subject: EU primary + APAC edge-cache and controlled DR routing proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@finserv-eu.com>, Yuki Nakamura <yuki.nakamura@acme-jp.co.jp>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 07:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU primary + APAC edge-cache and controlled DR routing proposal

Hi team —

Quick read: attached is a draft network proposal (network-draft-v2.pdf) and a simple traffic model (traffic-models.xlsx) that map expected request split for FinServ EU across EU primary and APAC edge-cache nodes. The ask from FinServ (see Claire) is that PII stays in-region and that failover to APAC only happens under strictly auditable conditions.

High-level proposal:
- EU region remains the primary for reads/writes for EU clients.
- APAC runs lightweight edge/cache nodes (no persistent customer PII store) to reduce latency for APAC-origin traffic and for read-only inference caching.
- During a regional outage, we perform a controlled DR cutover: 1) authorization from FinServ security lead, 2) enable APAC regional cache with read-only mode, 3) audit logs captured and retained, 4) post-cutover data purge confirmation.

Open design questions I want feedback on:
1) NAT / egress strategy for EU primary to ensure no cross-border persistent storage accidentally gets created.
2) How we gate ephemeral KV cache encryption keys so no KMS keys are replicated outside EU.
3) Acceptable SLA windows for automatic vs manual failover — FinServ prefers manual authorization.

Please review attached, comment inline in the Drive doc (link below), and flag any regulatory concerns.

Next steps I propose: short technical sync Fri 10:00 CET (30m) and attach the control-plane runbook we can hand to FinServ security.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@finserv-eu.com>, Yuki Nakamura <yuki.nakamura@acme-jp.co.jp>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 13:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU primary + APAC edge-cache and controlled DR routing proposal

Jordan — good draft, thanks. Quick notes after a read-through and a call with infra: 

- NAT / Egress: we should adopt a forced egress via EU-only NAT gateways pinned to the customer's VPC when operating in primary mode. For any APAC edge nodes, do not provision persistent volumes or object stores with EU-residency buckets. Edge caches must operate in-memory or ephemeral encrypted disk that is zeroed on shutdown.
- KMS gating: recommend customer-supplied KMS but using token-restricted temporary keys for edge caches; master key never leaves EU. We can implement a KMS-proxy in EU control plane to issue short-lived data keys for APAC edge.
- Failover model: since FinServ wants manual authorization, propose a two-step approval: (a) FinServ security (Claire) + Redwood on-call approve, (b) automated technical enablement (scripts that flip routing and start read-only caches). Log this as an auditable runbook step with an automatically captured request id.

I left inline comments in the PDF (page 4) about the expected cache TTLs and the traffic split assumptions in traffic-models.xlsx — looks like peak APAC traffic estimate may be 3-4x higher in local morning window (we should validate).

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thank you, Jordan and Marissa — this direction addresses many of our concerns. A couple of clarifications from our security/compliance team: 

1) If APAC is brought online for DR, FinServ requires a signed emergency exception with: scope, expected time window, and post-event data purge confirmation signed by Redwood. Can Redwood support an automated signed acknowledgement artifact?
2) We need an explicit list of what counts as "read-only" on the edge. Does any PII metadata (even hashed) ever persist?

We can do the short sync Friday 10:00 CET but prefer to have the runbook text available beforehand. Also cc'ing Yuki to confirm APAC timing constraints.

Regards,
Claire Dubois
Head of Security Operations | FinServ EU

Thanks all — short replies from APAC infra perspective: 
- Confirm APAC edge nodes can be configured with ephemeral-only caches and disabled persistence. We can bake automation to trigger a cryptographic nonce on failover that forces the cache to mount read-only and self-destruct after X hours.
- We will need the exact list of KMS operations you expect to proxy (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) so we can scope IAM for the APAC control-plane.
- Friday 10:00 CET works for me (19:00 JST) — will join.

Yuki
Head of Cloud Operations | Acme JP (partner infra)
summary: Thread discussing a proposed architecture that keeps EU as primary while running APAC as ephemeral edge caches, gating KMS access, and defining a manual/ auditable DR cutover for a FinServ EU customer. Attachments include a network design draft and a traffic model. Action: review runbook and confirm KMS scoping + emergency exception artifact.
